Based on the material provided, here is the answer to your question:

### What Part 5.2 Requires

**CIP-007-6 Requirement R5, Part 5.2** requires the Responsible Entity to **identify and inventory all known enabled default or other generic account types**.

The specific regulatory text states:
> "5.2 Where possible, default and other generic accounts provided by a vendor should be removed, renamed, or disabled prior to production use of the Cyber Asset or BES Cyber System. If this is not possible, the passwords must be changed from the default provided by the vendor. Default and other generic accounts remaining enabled must be documented. For common configurations, this documentation can be performed at a BES Cyber System or more general level." [csection-babf06d3f1ed425a7b4a]

The standard further clarifies in the **Measures** table that the entity must:
> "Identify and inventory all known enabled default or other generic account types, either by system, by groups of systems, by location, or by system type(s)." [csection-ec458b69bb605a5c345a]

The rationale explains that this is done to ensure entities understand the risk these accounts pose, noting that "Identifying the use of default or generic account types that could introduce vulnerabilities has the benefit ensuring entities understand the possible risk these accounts pose to the BES Cyber System." [csection-2bf8f38b1549dcff2970]

### Which Document Shows That We Actually Do It

The operator's document that demonstrates compliance with this requirement is the **CIP Cyber Security Policy**, specifically section **3.4.5 System Access Controls Process (R5)**.

This document explicitly states that the entity (LSPG) shall:
> "Identify and inventory all known enabled default or other generic account types, either by system, by groups of systems, by location, or by system type(s) (Part 5.2)" [isection-fbc9ce9e2439c4f4af90]

This policy section directly maps the operator's internal process to the specific requirement of CIP-007-6 R5 Part 5.2.
